claims.statement: Clicking a session row reaches the kernel through the single bridge method `session/focus`, whose request carries only the scanner-derived tool name and whose response carries `{ ok, action, error?, hwnd? }`; the outcome travels only in that response, with no corresponding push event and nothing in `panel/changed` reflecting it.

Using the tool name as a map key is the arbitrary-path defence: `FocusService.focusTool` resolves it only when it is an own property of the loaded tool map, so unknown names, path-shaped payloads (`C:\Windows\System32\cmd.exe`, `../../evil.exe`) and prototype members (`toString`, `constructor`, `valueOf`) never become an execution target and degrade instead.

`planFocus(raw, windows)` is a pure decision kernel returning an exhaustive three-state result — `focus` with hwnd and pid, `launch` with the configured exe, or `degrade` with a reason — so the caller has no fallback branch to forget; unknown tools, malformed mappings and a blank launch target all degrade rather than throw.

`asToolTarget` is the second guard on the tool map: it accepts only a non-null object with a string `launch` and an array of strings in `processes`, which converts a prototype-chain hit or a malformed config entry into the same silent degrade instead of a `TypeError` thrown from `target.processes.map`.

Window selection ranks visible non-minimized windows (score 2) above visible minimized ones (score 1), skips invisible windows entirely (score -1, so a tray-resident tool goes down the launch path), resolves ties by enumeration order (topmost z-order first), and matches by exact equality of the normalised image name against `target.processes` with no prefix or fuzzy matching.

`normalizeProcessName` in `config.ts` (basename, lowercase, strip `.exe`) is the single implementation of process-name normalisation, applied both at config load by `mergeTools` (normalising and de-duplicating user-supplied `processes` strings) and at match time in `pickWindow`; `focus/plan.ts` imports it rather than re-implementing it because two copies would drift.

`%VAR%` expansion is a service-level concern applied immediately before launching, using the injected `env` (production `process.env`): `planFocus` returns the configured launch string unexpanded, unknown placeholders are left verbatim, and the production adapter launches via `shell.openPath` with ShellExecute semantics (so a single-instance app is raised rather than duplicated).

A window-enumeration failure is non-fatal: `FocusService.focusTool` catches `listWindows()` throwing, logs a `deck-focus: 窗口枚举失败，降级为仅启动` warning and continues with an empty snapshot, so a tool that is not running can still be launched from the same click.

Each native outcome has its own degrade branch inside `focusTool`: a `false` return from the focus adapter (the foreground lock refusing `SetForegroundWindow`) becomes `系统拒绝置前该窗口（前台锁）`, a thrown focus error becomes `置前异常：…`, a non-empty `shell.openPath` error string is passed through verbatim as the reason, and a rejecting launch becomes `启动失败：…`; `ok` is true only for the `focused` and `launched` actions.

Silent degradation is deliberate for this workflow: the service's boundary comment and the card's header both state that clicking a session row is a light interaction, so a failure must not break the panel, pop a dialog or interrupt the desktop; the renderer therefore never branches on the result beyond recording it and has no error UI, retry or toast.

Because failures are invisible on screen, the observability of this path is entirely evidence records: the card emits `session-focus-clicked { tool, id }` before the call and `session-focus-result { tool, id, ok, action, error, hwnd }` after it — with `error` and `hwnd` explicitly null when absent and `hwnd` recorded as a decimal handle — plus `session-focus-failed { tool, id, message }` on a rejection; the main process appends each to the JSONL event log when `DECK_EVENT_LOG` is set.

In-band degradation is a resolved response rather than a rejection: `session/focus` with an unknown tool resolves to `{ ok: false, action: 'degraded' }` and the panel still answers other methods afterwards, which is why the renderer needs no try/catch; only transport-level failures (the ok/error envelope in `panel-ipc.ts` rethrown by the preload bridge) reject the promise.

The Windows adapter is the only FFI owner on this path: it binds `user32.dll`/`kernel32.dll` lazily and memoizes inside the first call (so injected fake sources never load native code), enumerates top-level windows with the `GetTopWindow`/`GetWindow(GW_HWNDNEXT)` chain under a 2048-iteration guard rather than an `EnumWindows` callback, and its candidate shape (`hwnd`, `pid`, exe basename, `visible`, `minimized`) deliberately carries no window title, matching the privacy boundary that only the owning process's image name is read.

Rows are only clickable where the page declares a hotzone: the panel window is click-through (`setIgnoreMouseEvents(true)`) except inside declared rectangles, and `declareHotZones()` declares one rectangle per `.card` element, so `#sessions-card` is the addressable region and rows need no rectangles of their own; separately, `sessions.slice(0, 9)` means a session beyond the ninth has no DOM row to click at all.

The card publishes `sessions-rendered { n, count, rows }` on the first three renders after mount, carrying each row's `tool`, `project` and client rectangle; this is how the acceptance battery locates a specific session row to click without any accessibility API, and how it distinguishes "row not found" from "click never arrived".

`config.tools` is the entire configuration surface of this workflow — per tool a `launch` path (with `%VAR%` placeholders) and `processes` image names to match; the map is loaded once at boot (`loadConfig` on `app.getAppPath()/config.json`, then handed to the kernel as `focus: { tools: config.tools }`), so changing it requires a panel restart, and because the settings slider persists by rewriting the whole config file from the same in-memory object, a hand edit made while the panel runs can be overwritten by the next opacity change.

A missing or partial `tools` section is tolerated rather than fatal: `mergeTools` starts from `defaultTools()` and overlays the file field by field with warnings, and `FocusService` falls back to the same `defaultTools()` when constructed without a `tools` option, so a config-less boot does not degrade every click; `processes` entries list both launcher and application image names because those can differ for the same tool.

The routing key `SessionInfo.tool` couples two independently defined maps — the scanner keys and the `config.tools` keys are the same five names and nothing cross-references them — so a rename on one side surfaces only as an unmapped two-letter tag (`??`) plus a degraded click.

`FocusDeps` (`listWindows`, `focusWindow`, `launch`, `env`) is the injection seam that lets both the unit suite and the bridge contract suite drive the whole focus/launch/degrade state machine without FFI or real tools, and `toolsForTest()` is the observation seam exposing the effective tool map.
